keys.description: Show first-run setup on startup. Missing or true shows onboarding; continuing from onboarding writes onboarding = false.

Allowed models per worker kind, for example claude = ["fable", "opus", "sonnet"]. A missing or empty list allows any model. Model overrides apply to Claude and Codex workers.

Claude --permission-mode for Orbit workers when orbit_agent_start names none: manual, acceptEdits, auto, plan, or dontAsk. Unset inherits your Claude settings. bypassPermissions is refused. Applies to Claude workers on config reload.

Orbit events that notify you through ui.toast.delivery: a worker report delivered to Polaris, an Aster notice (worker lost, unreported, or timed out), a worker blocked on a prompt for 30 seconds, and a failed delivery. One notification per task and event; an empty list disables them. Nothing is shown while ui.toast.delivery is off.
How long a queued Orbit report waits while Polaris is absent or its pane does not run its agent before the delivery fails and you are notified (milliseconds, at least 1000).
Allow Polaris to answer a blocked Orbit worker's approval prompt with orbit_agent_approve or orbit_agent_deny. When false, those tools refuse and Polaris asks you to answer in the worker's pane.
Where decisions beyond the rules come from: rules (never calls out) or jev (TypeSafe AI's Jev model over HTTPS). The rules for worker approvals always run first.
Jev model name.
Environment variable of the Aster server holding the API key. Key material is never logged, journaled, or shown in activity.
File holding the API key, read when api_key_env is unset; ~ is expanded. Refused unless it is a regular file that group and others cannot read (chmod 600).
API base URL: https, or http only for 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
Limit of one provider call in milliseconds, 100 to 30000. A timeout counts as no answer: the user is asked.
Ask the provider about worker permission prompts no rule decides. Decisions are only made while polaris.approvals.lead_may_approve is true.
Minimum probability of approve for an automatic approval.
Maximum combined probability of ask_user and deny for an automatic approval.
Minimum risk probability in levels 0 and 1 (read-only, low risk) for an automatic approval.
Maximum risk probability in levels 3 and 4 (sensitive, destructive) for an automatic approval.
Whole simple commands the rules approve; * matches any text. A command with shell operators, redirections, or substitutions never matches.

keys.description: Text that always sends a prompt to the user, matched anywhere in the command ignoring case; * matches any text. Checked before allow_patterns. Never denies automatically.
Check each worker report against its assignment with the provider and add a Decision line to flagged reports. Never blocks delivery.
needs_followup at or above this flags a report.
answers_assignment score (0 to 4) below this flags a report.
Let orbit_route ask the provider which team role should own a request. Suggestions only; nothing is assigned.
Minimum owner probability for orbit_route to return accepted true.
Before typing a report batch into an idle Polaris, ask whether to deliver now. A low answer defers delivery by 30 seconds; it never delivers earlier.
deliver_now below this defers delivery by 30 seconds.

Pinned team roles, present in every session's Orbit team roster: merged into orbit-team.json at each session start and on config reload (area, prompt, and members follow config; members keep their terminals and sessions; members removed from config are released). Each [[polaris.team]] entry has name (lowercase, like an agent name), area (free text), prompt (role instructions, at most 4096 bytes), members: 1 to 4 tables with name, kind (claude or codex), and optional model and permission_mode, checked against [polaris.workers], and an optional pipeline, a list of kinds such as ["claude", "codex"] that a task relayed within the role passes through (the first kind starts the task; each handoff without an explicit target goes to the next kind). An optional integrator names the member who integrates the patches of the role's parallel steps, applies them with git apply --3way, resolves conflicts and runs the full tests (default: the first member of the reviewer role, else the role's first member). At most 8 roles. Each role gets its own tab before the Orbit tab; its members are resumed after a restart and relaunched when their agent exits. Polaris cannot remove a pinned role (orbit_role_pinned); orbit_team_define may add members or override its prompt for the current session only. A role removed from config stays in the session, unpinned.

Text conditions optionally accept ignore_case for ASCII matching; numeric conditions require full finite numbers. state_icon accepts fixed styles only. At most 16 rows and 16 tokens per row.

Expose the focused pane's cursor anchor to the outer terminal even when the pane requested `?25l`, so macOS native input methods keep tracking the candidate window when TUIs paint their own cursor (Claude Code, pi, codex, etc.). Default: false.  When the pane reports no cursor position, falls back to the pane's top-left so a stable IME anchor is always available.  Trade-off when enabled: an extra hardware cursor will be visible in the outer terminal for apps that hide the cursor without painting a replacement (vim normal mode, etc.). See #149.

Restrict `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` to focused panes whose detected agent matches one of these names (case-insensitive). Empty list means apply to any focused pane. Unknown agent names are ignored; if the list contains no valid names, the reveal does not apply. Accepted names: pi, claude, codex, gemini, cursor, devin, cline, opencode, copilot, kimi, kiro, droid, amp, grok, hermes, kilo, qodercli, qoder, qwen, qwen-code, letta, letta-code, maki.
Cursor shape rendered for the IME anchor when `reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime` is enabled.

While prefix mode is active, temporarily switch the host input source to an ASCII-capable mode so prefix commands are read as ASCII even when an IME is active, then restore the previous input source when prefix mode exits. On macOS this selects the ASCII-capable keyboard layout; on Windows it switches the IME to English (ASCII) input. Windows support is currently limited to the Korean IME; with an IME for any other language, the input source is left unchanged. macOS and Windows only; a no-op elsewhere and a best-effort no-op if the switch fails.
